content: The WikiDoc Scholars Program is designed to provide a transparent and objective evaluation of your performance as a participant. This document serves as a self-assessment tool and a guide for continuous improvement. Throughout the year, you are encouraged to print this document and highlight the metrics that best represent your contributions to WikiDoc. You are solely responsible for determining the trajectory of your performance, whether it is below average (D), average (C), good (B), or excellent (A). Your academic performance, both in quality and quantity, will significantly influence your career trajectory. For instance, matching into a U.S. community hospital residency program may be a stretch goal unless you achieve exceptionally high percentiles on your USMLE exams. To request a letter of recommendation, you should provide an updated CV and a list of topics that best represent your work. Objective Metrics for Letters of Recommendation Depending on your career path at WikiDoc, the following metrics may be included in your recommendation letter: Participation in the WikiDoc Scholars Program for a specified duration. Completion of topics within the differential project. Contribution to chapters in the Resident Survival Guide. Completion of board review questions. Certification as an angiographer. Interpretation of a specified number of films. Work Product Quality Poor Quality: Frequent typographical and formatting errors, lack of attention to capitalization, and failure to follow templates, necessitating extensive revisions. Such individuals may be more of a liability than an asset. Needs Improvement: Inconsistent attention to detail, occasional errors, and incomplete or late submissions. Meets Requirements: Work is completed on time with minimal errors and does not require constant supervision. Exceeds Requirements: Consistently high-quality work, with minimal need for corrections, and a proactive approach to improving performance. Outstanding: Less than 1% error rate, excellent accuracy, and exceptional attention to detail. Work Ethic and Quantity Poor: Poor time management, frequent absences, and distractions such as social media or gaming during work hours. Such behavior may compromise patient care. Needs Improvement: Inconsistent attendance and productivity, with occasional lapses in prioritizing tasks. Meets Requirements: Satisfactory work ethic, consistent attendance, and appropriate workplace behavior. Exceeds Requirements: Strong work ethic, often working beyond standard hours, and demonstrating a commitment to professional growth. Outstanding: Exceptional dedication, often working seven days a week, and consistently exceeding expectations. Dependability Poor: Frequent unapproved absences, tardiness, and early departures, which may lead to adverse patient outcomes. Needs Improvement: Occasional lapses in attendance or failure to complete tasks before leaving. Meets Requirements: Consistently punctual, reliable, and responsible in covering duties. Exceeds Requirements: Excellent attendance record and willingness to take on additional responsibilities. Outstanding: Always present and on time, with no unscheduled absences, and a proactive approach to ensuring team success. Cooperativeness Poor: Displays superiority, negativity, and lack of empathy, often creating a divisive work environment. Needs Improvement: Occasional negativity and reluctance to assist others. Meets Requirements: Friendly and respectful interactions with peers, clinical sites, and sponsors. Exceeds Requirements: A team player who has evolved into a team leader, demonstrating honesty and politeness. Outstanding: A natural leader who inspires and uplifts the team, fostering a positive and collaborative environment. Adaptability Poor: Requires constant supervision and struggles with unexpected situations, which may hinder residency training. Needs Improvement: Difficulty in making sound decisions under unusual circumstances. Meets Requirements: Adjusts to changes as expected and maintains composure during stressful situations. Exceeds Requirements: Proactively proposes solutions and adjusts priorities effectively. Outstanding: Adapts well to new systems, seeks training to enhance skills, and knows when to seek help, ensuring success as a resident. Communication Poor: Delayed or incomplete reports, condescending tone, and poor phone etiquette. Needs Improvement: Unclear or incomplete messages and occasional complaints from collaborators. Meets Requirements: Polite and professional communication, with accurate and well-written reports. Exceeds Requirements: Adopts the organization’s writing style and independently addresses queries with maturity. Outstanding: Demonstrates emotional intelligence, excellent oral and written communication skills, and a natural ability to engage large audiences. Decision-Making and Problem-Solving Poor: Frequently arrives at incorrect conclusions due to faulty information processing and lacks planning skills. Needs Improvement: Struggles to prioritize and focus on critical aspects of tasks. Meets Requirements: Offers workable solutions and uses good judgment in problem-solving. Exceeds Requirements: Strong analytical skills and the ability to identify root causes of problems. Outstanding: Proactively prevents problems, gathers high-quality data, and demonstrates exceptional situational awareness. Service to Clinical Sites, Sponsors, and Collaborators Poor: Rude and unprofessional behavior, with poor relationship skills and a lack of trustworthiness. Needs Improvement: Annoyance with collaborators and failure to follow through on requests. Meets Requirements: Maintains professionalism and tries to be helpful to collaborators. Exceeds Requirements: Courteous, prompt, and accurate in addressing questions. Outstanding: Consistently follows through on commitments and receives praise for attention to detail. Use of Equipment and Materials Poor: Misuse of equipment, leading to damage or loss, and failure to maintain security protocols. Needs Improvement: Occasional lapses in equipment care and maintenance. Meets Requirements: Takes good care of equipment and uses supplies efficiently. Exceeds Requirements: Quickly masters new software and independently troubleshoots IT issues. Outstanding: Develops innovative solutions and efficiently resolves hardware/software problems. Project Management Poor: Lack of follow-through, poor planning, and failure to meet deadlines. Needs Improvement: Poorly designed project plans and failure to communicate potential issues. Meets Requirements: Prepares detailed project plans and monitors progress effectively. Exceeds Requirements: Proactively identifies barriers and contributes to scientific discussions. Outstanding: Functions in a leadership capacity, preparing charters and manuscripts independently. Leadership Skills Poor: Dictatorial approach, lack of emotional intelligence, and inability to lead a team. Needs Improvement: Impatience and lack of training for subordinates. Meets Requirements: Fair and effective team leadership, with an open-door policy. Exceeds Requirements: Confidently leads teams to complete projects with minimal oversight. Outstanding: Leads by example, inspires others, and demonstrates exceptional emotional intelligence and vision. Summary Statement The summary statement for your performance will reflect your achievements and contributions during the WikiDoc Scholars Program. It may range from meeting basic requirements to exceeding expectations and demonstrating exceptional potential for success in a residency program.
